The server decides TLS by reading the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header (set by the reverse proxy) in the `req.protocol`/`req.secure` getters of `lib/request.js`, but only after verifying via the compiled trust-proxy function that the proxy is a trusted hop; `lib/utils.js` compiles that trust function and `lib/application.js` wires it into the app settings.

The server's `protocol` getter in `lib/request.js` reads `this.socket.encrypted`, and only if the `trust proxy` setting's compiled function trusts the socket's remote address does it trust and use the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header (so a reverse proxy that terminates TLS can report `https`), mirroring that logic in the `host`/`ips` getters.

The server combines `req.socket.encrypted` with the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header, but only honors the header when the peer socket address is trusted by the "trust proxy" function.

- `lib/request.js` — the `protocol` getter: starts from `this.socket.encrypted ? 'https' : 'http'`; if the "trust proxy fn" does not trust `this.socket.remoteAddress`, it returns that directly; otherwise it reads `X-Forwarded-Proto` (taking the first value before any comma) and returns it. The `secure` getter is just `protocol === 'https'`, and `host` uses the same trust check for `X-Forwarded-Host`.
- `lib/utils.js` — `compileTrust` turns the `trust proxy` setting (`true`, hop count, comma-separated addresses/subnets, or function) into that trust function via `proxyaddr.compile`.
- `lib/application.js` — the application-level default for the `trust proxy` setting and where the compiled "trust proxy fn" is installed.
- `test/req.protocol.js` — tests confirming `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` yields `https` only when `trust proxy` is enabled.
- `lib/express.js` — exposes the app settings (`enable('trust proxy')`) used to configure this behavior.

So when a reverse proxy terminates TLS, the backend sees a plain socket (`socket.encrypted` false) unless the proxy address is trusted, in which case the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header the proxy injected decides `req.protocol`/`req.secure`.

The `protocol` getter in `lib/request.js` falls back to the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header (set by the terminating proxy) when the `trust proxy` setting is enabled, with that setting compiled in `lib/application.js` via `compileTrust` in `lib/utils.js`.
